title: Understanding models (E1/E2/E3 & Maxx)
content:
## What E1, E2, E3 are

Emergent uses a **tiered model system** to give you control over agent intelligence and credit consumption. Each tier—**E1**, **E2**, **E3**—represents a different underlying language model with distinct capabilities, speed, and cost.

- **E1** — The fastest, most efficient tier. Best for small edits, bug fixes, or when you want to iterate quickly on straightforward changes. Consumes the fewest credits.
- **E2** — A balanced middle tier. Suitable for most day-to-day building: adding features, refactoring components, implementing standard integrations. Good quality-to-cost ratio.
- **E3** — The most capable tier. Use this when you need deep reasoning, complex architectural decisions, or are working through ambiguous requirements. Consumes the most credits per job.

<Tip title="Start with E2">
For most prompts, **E2** strikes the right balance. Drop to **E1** for trivial changes; escalate to **E3** only when the agent struggles or you're tackling a genuinely hard problem.
</Tip>

### When to use which tier

| Tier | Best for | Credit impact |
|------|----------|---------------|
| **E1** | Quick fixes, typos, small CSS tweaks, simple config changes | Lowest |
| **E2** | New components, API integrations, moderate refactors | Medium |
| **E3** | Complex logic, debugging subtle issues, architectural planning | Highest |

You select the tier **before submitting your prompt** in the chat interface. The platform displays the current tier above the prompt input; click it to switch. Once a job starts, it runs on the chosen tier for its entire workflow.

<Note>
The agent's [workflow](/how-the-agent-runs-workflow-stop-reasons) (plan → code → test → review) is the same across all tiers—only the underlying model's reasoning depth changes.
</Note>

---

## Maxx mode & its credit impact

**Maxx mode** is an optional power-user setting that removes the agent's internal token budget limits, allowing it to produce **longer plans, more comprehensive code changes, and deeper test coverage** in a single job.

When Maxx is **off** (the default), the agent operates within normal context windows and stops after a reasonable number of iterations. This keeps jobs predictable and credit-efficient.

When Maxx is **on**, the agent can:
- Generate multi-file, sweeping refactors in one pass
- Write exhaustive test suites
- Tackle extremely large prompts or complex multi-step features

<Warning title="Maxx consumes significantly more credits">
A single Maxx-enabled job can use **3–10× the credits** of a normal job on the same tier, because the agent makes more LLM calls, processes larger contexts, and iterates more deeply. Use Maxx **sparingly**—only when you genuinely need the extra horsepower.
</Warning>

### When to enable Maxx

<Steps>
<Step title="Identify the need">
Ask yourself: *Is this prompt too broad or complex for a normal job?* If the agent has been stopping prematurely or you're refactoring an entire module, Maxx may help.
</Step>

<Step title="Enable before submitting">
Toggle Maxx mode in the prompt interface (next to the model tier selector). It applies only to the **next job** you start.
</Step>

<Step title="Monitor credit usage">
Check your [credit balance](/how-credits-work) after the job completes. If Maxx burned through more than expected, consider breaking future large prompts into smaller, sequential jobs.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
Maxx mode works with **any tier** (E1, E2, or E3). Combining **E3 + Maxx** gives you maximum capability but also maximum cost—reserve this for truly challenging scenarios.
</Info>

---

## Choosing the right combination

A quick decision tree:

- **Small, obvious change?** → E1, Maxx off.
- **Standard feature or integration?** → E2, Maxx off.
- **Large refactor or ambitious new subsystem?** → E2 or E3, Maxx on (but watch credits).
- **Agent keeps stopping short of a solution?** → Try the next tier up, or enable Maxx, then re-prompt.

You can always adjust mid-conversation: if a job on E2 didn't produce the depth you needed, follow up with the same prompt on E3 or with Maxx enabled. The platform retains your chat context, so the agent understands what you've already tried.

<Tip title="Iterate cheaply first">
Start with a lower tier and Maxx off. If the result isn't quite right, your follow-up prompt costs less than if you'd gone straight to E3 + Maxx and overshot.
</Tip>
